info.title: E-Motion Controller Protocol
info.description:
The contract between E-Motion Studio and an E-Motion robot controller.

## Layering

This document describes the JSON-RPC 2.0 method surface only. The full stack is:

  - RFC 6455 WebSocket for transport, framing, and liveness. Liveness is the
    standard ping/pause frame pair at the transport layer; there is deliberately
    no application-level heartbeat method.
  - JSON-RPC 2.0 for envelope, correlation, and errors.
  - This document (OpenRPC 1.4) for the interface contract.

Bulk transfer - program upload, log and trace download, firmware - is NOT here.
It is served over plain HTTP on the same host so that it stays curl-able and does
not occupy the live link. See `x-bulkTransfer` below.

## Who may call what

Most methods are Studio to controller. Methods marked
`x-messageDirection: serverToClient` are sent by the controller and are always
JSON-RPC notifications (no `id`, no response). OpenRPC 1.4 has no first-class
representation for server-initiated messages, so they are declared as methods
with a null result and tagged with an extension field. This is a known gap in
OpenRPC, not an accident of this document.

## Units

Every quantity on the wire is SI. Lengths are metres, angles are radians, time is
seconds, and rates are per second. There is no unit field anywhere in this
protocol and there must never be one - the unit is carried by the schema type
name. Conversion to and from display units is a presentation concern and belongs
in the client.

## What this protocol is not

It is not a safety function. `motion/stop` is a convenience that asks a working
controller over a working network to decelerate. The safety-rated stop is a
physical circuit that keeps working when this link is dead, the controller has
wedged, and the switch has been unplugged. Nothing in this document may be
relied upon to prevent injury.

It is also not a servo loop. Trajectory execution happens entirely on the
controller. The Studio starts and stops motions and observes them; it is never
between the planner and the drives. A Studio that disconnects mid-motion must be
a non-event for the robot.

servers.name: controller
servers.summary: A controller on the local network
servers.description:
Controllers advertise themselves over mDNS as `_emotion._tcp`. The
Studio browses for them rather than asking the operator for an address.

host.description: Hostname or address of the controller.

port.description: TCP port of the controller's WebSocket endpoint.

x-bulkTransfer.description: Large or infrequent payloads are served over HTTP on the same host, not over this link.

endpoints.PUT /api/programs/{id}: Upload or replace a program source.
endpoints.GET /api/traces/{motionId}: Download the full-rate trace of a completed motion.

x-conflation.description: Subscription streams are conflated, never queued. When the client is slower than the stream rate the controller REPLACES the pending frame rather than buffering behind it, so the client always receives the most recent state and never falls progressively further behind. Dropped intermediate frames are expected and are not an error. This is a stated property of the protocol: an implementation that buffers stream frames is non-conformant. Events (`notifications/events/emitted`) are NOT conflated - see `events/since`.

methods.name: initialize
methods.description:
The first message on every connection. No other method may be called until
this has returned and the client has sent `notifications/initialized`.

The client offers the newest protocol version it speaks. If the controller
speaks that version it echoes it back. If it does not, it returns the newest
version it does speak, and the client decides whether it can proceed or must
tell the operator to update something. The controller never guesses.

Capabilities exist so that a newer Studio can discover what an older controller
supports without probing for it and interpreting the failures.

params.name: protocolVersion
params.summary: Newest protocol version the client speaks.

params.name: capabilities
params.summary: What the client is able to receive.

methods.name: notifications/initialized
methods.description:
Sent as a JSON-RPC notification once the client has accepted the result of
`initialize`. The controller treats the session as usable from this point.

methods.name: robot/describe
methods.summary: Static description of the robot: kinematics, limits, frames.
methods.description:
Everything that does not change while the controller is running. The Studio
fetches this once after initialize and caches it. If it ever does change - a
tool is reconfigured, a joint limit is edited - the controller emits
`notifications/robot/describeChanged` and the Studio refetches.

methods.name: notifications/robot/describeChanged
methods.summary: The static description is stale; refetch it.
methods.description:
Deliberately carries no payload. The Studio calls `robot/describe` again
rather than trying to apply a diff, because the description is small and a
wrong diff is worse than a redundant fetch.

methods.name: robot/state
methods.description:
For clients that want a snapshot without subscribing - a script, a health
check, a freshly opened panel. Anything drawing continuously should subscribe
instead of polling this.

methods.name: streams/subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribe to one or more conflated state streams.
methods.description:
The returned `subscriptionId` is the topic handle: every
`notifications/streams/update` carries it, and it is what you pass to
`streams/unsubscribe`.

The requested rate is advisory. The controller returns the rate it will
actually send at, which may be lower - it will not exceed the `maxRateHz` it
advertised at initialize, and it may reduce further under load. Clients must
read the granted rate rather than assuming they got what they asked for.

Streams are conflated. See `x-conflation` at the top of this document; the
summary is that a slow client receives the newest frame and misses the ones in
between, by design.

params.name: rateHz
params.summary: Requested update rate. Advisory; see the granted rate in the result.

rateHz.description: The rate the controller will actually send at.

methods.name: streams/unsubscribe
methods.description:
Idempotent: unsubscribing an unknown or already-ended subscription succeeds.
A client tearing down after a reconnect should not have to reason about whether
the controller already dropped it.

methods.name: notifications/streams/update
methods.description:
Carries the newest value of one stream. `seq` is monotonic per subscription
and per stream, and it SKIPS - a gap means frames were conflated away, which is
normal and must not be treated as an error or trigger a resync. If you need
every sample, download the trace over HTTP after the motion completes.

params.name: seq
params.summary: Monotonic, with gaps where frames were conflated away.

methods.name: notifications/events/emitted
methods.summary: A discrete event: fault, mode change, program lifecycle.
methods.description:
Events are NOT conflated and must not be lost. Every event carries a
monotonic `seq` with no gaps. A client that sees a gap has missed events and
must call `events/since` to fill it - that is the entire reason the sequence
number exists.

A fault is an event, not a stream. Never infer a fault from the absence of a
stream frame.

methods.name: events/since
methods.description:
Called after a reconnect, or on noticing a gap in event sequence numbers.
Returns every event with `seq` strictly greater than the one supplied, oldest
first.

The controller keeps a bounded replay buffer whose depth it advertised at
initialize. If the requested sequence has fallen out of it, this fails with
`SequenceUnavailable` rather than silently returning a partial history - a
client that cannot prove it has seen every fault must say so to the operator
rather than pretend.

params.name: seq
params.summary: Last sequence number the client has definitely seen.

latestSeq.description: Newest sequence number the controller holds.

complete.description: False when `limit` truncated the reply; call again from the last returned seq.

methods.name: motion/jog
methods.summary: Jog a single joint under a deadman timeout.
methods.description:
Deliberately self-cancelling. The controller decelerates to a stop when
`timeout` elapses without a further jog call for the same joint, so a Studio
that crashes, a laptop lid that closes, or a network that drops mid-jog leaves
the robot stationary rather than moving.

The client refreshes by calling again while the operator holds the control.
`motion/stop` ends it early. There is no separate jog-stop method, because a
protocol where stopping requires a message to arrive is a protocol where
stopping fails when the message does not.

This is a convenience for operators at a keyboard. It is not a safety function.

params.name: velocity
params.summary: Signed. Magnitude is clamped to the joint's configured jog limit.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: Deadman interval. The controller stops if not refreshed within this.

velocity.description: The velocity actually applied, after clamping.

methods.name: motion/moveJoint
methods.description:
Returns as soon as the motion is accepted and planned, not when it finishes.
Progress arrives as `notifications/progress` against the `progressToken`, and
completion arrives as an event. The call may be cancelled with
`notifications/cancelled` carrying this request's id.

The target is validated against joint limits before acceptance, so an
out-of-range target is an error rather than a motion that faults partway.

params.name: maxVelocity
params.summary: Per-joint ceiling. Clamped to configured limits.

params.name: progressToken
params.summary: Opaque client token echoed in progress notifications.

methods.name: motion/stop
methods.summary: Ask the controller to stop moving. NOT a safety function.
methods.description:
`controlled` decelerates on the planned path and leaves the servos enabled.
`immediate` decelerates at the drives' maximum rate, which may deviate from the
path.

Read this twice: this method asks a working controller, over a working network,
to stop. It cannot help when the controller has wedged, the link is down, or
the operator is in the cell. The safety-rated stop is a physical circuit and
this method is not a substitute for it, an implementation of it, or a fallback
for it.

methods.name: programs/list
methods.summary: List programs stored on the controller.
methods.description: Metadata only. Source is fetched over HTTP - see `x-bulkTransfer`.

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque cursor from a previous reply.

methods.name: programs/run
methods.description:
Returns when the program has been accepted and started, not when it
completes. Lifecycle arrives as events and progress as
`notifications/progress`.

The program runs entirely on the controller. If the Studio disconnects the
program continues - which is the correct behaviour for offline programming and
the reason this is not a streaming call.

methods.name: notifications/progress
methods.description:
Echoes the `progressToken` supplied by the caller. `total` may be absent
when the controller cannot know the extent in advance.

methods.name: notifications/cancelled
methods.description:
Best effort. The request may already have completed, in which case this is
ignored. A cancelled motion decelerates in the same way as
`motion/stop` with mode `controlled`.

The controller does not send a JSON-RPC response for a request cancelled this
way; the client must treat the cancellation as terminal for that id.

params.name: requestId
params.summary: The `id` of the JSON-RPC request being cancelled.

ProtocolVersion.description:
Date-stamped protocol revision, e.g. `2026-08-14`. Compared for equality,
not ordered - a controller either speaks a revision or it does not.

ClientCapabilities.description:
Presence of a key means the client supports the feature. Empty objects are
deliberate: they leave room for per-feature options later without a breaking
change.

replayDepth.description: How many events the controller retains for `events/since`.

Metres.description: Length in metres. SI on the wire, always.

Radians.description: Angle in radians. SI on the wire, always.

RadiansPerSecond.description: Angular velocity in radians per second.

RadiansPerSecondSquared.description: Angular acceleration in radians per second squared.

Timestamp.description:
RFC 3339 with at least millisecond precision, from the controller's clock.
Clients must not assume the controller's clock agrees with their own; use it for
ordering and for measuring intervals, not for absolute correlation with desktop
events.

JointVector.description:
Joint positions in the order given by `robot/describe`. Length always equals
the robot's degrees of freedom.

Pose.description:
A rigid transform. Rotation is intrinsic RPY about X, Y, then Z, matching
the convention used throughout E-Motion. Stated here explicitly because a pose
with an unstated rotation convention is a defect waiting to happen.

axis.description: Unit axis of rotation or translation in the joint's own frame.

baseFrame.description: Robot base relative to the cell origin.

toolFrame.description: Tool centre point relative to the final link.

RobotMode.description:
`estopped` reflects an observed hardware state. It is reported, never
commanded - nothing in this protocol may assert or clear it.

estop.description: True when the safety circuit is open. Observed, not commanded.

StreamPayload.description: Discriminated by the `stream` field of the enclosing notification.

seq.description:
Monotonic and gapless. A gap means the client missed events; call
`events/since`.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable identifier, e.g. `drive.overtemperature`. Clients
branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable, may be localised, may change between firmware versions.

active.description: For latching faults: whether the condition is still present.

SubscriptionId.description:
Opaque handle. Also serves as the topic identifier - there is no separate
topic concept in this protocol.

NotInitialized.message: Session not initialized; call initialize first.

AlreadyInitialized.message: Session already initialized on this connection.

RobotNotReady.message: Robot is not in a state that accepts this command.

SafetyStopActive.message: Safety circuit is open; motion commands are refused.

LimitExceeded.message: Requested target or rate exceeds a configured limit.

MotionInProgress.message: Another motion is executing; stop or cancel it first.

UnknownJoint.message: No such joint on this robot.

UnknownStream.message: No such stream on this controller.

TooManySubscriptions.message: Subscription limit reached for this connection.

SequenceUnavailable.message: Requested sequence has fallen out of the replay buffer.

ProgramNotFound.message: No such program on this controller.
